end.summary:
Practised plant-eaters, meat-eaters, and animals that eat both.
Built and read simple food chains; 2 of 3 attempts were unaided correct.
Predicted that fewer larvae would mean less food for fish.
Arrow meaning was mixed up: Manav said it points from the eater to its food; this was not corrected later.
end.parentNote: Asha practised animal diets, food-chain arrows, and what happens when one part of a chain is removed. Manav correctly gave examples such as deer eating grass and read chains including “algae → larvae → fish”; they also explained that fewer larvae would leave fish with less food. The arrow direction was still mixed up, so at home, ask them to say “the arrow points to the eater” while building chains such as grass → deer → lion.
